newsitem.title: UK: Options - Focus shifts to puts in soft commodities.
newsitem.headline: Options - Focus shifts to puts in soft commodities.

text.p: Puts garnered most of the business in coffee and cocoa options this week and volatilies came under pressure as players kept their distance from rangebound futures.

Market makers noted on Thursday buying and selling at- or near-the-money puts were the main interest in otherwise sagging turnover, reflecting the bearish sentiment in coffee and cocoa futures recently.
Buying in coffee puts centred around the $1,400 strike which now controls half of the total open interest in puts. Also active were $1,350 and $1,300 at stable volatilities of 27-29 percent.
"Either they want to protect their position or they are bearish. A lot of people are long of the puts," said one trader.
Coffee futures pulled back sharply this week to trade around $1,380 and near the closely-watched $1,360 support on talk of growing robusta supplies, mainly from the Far Eastern origins.
The market had earlier moved up to above the $1,400 mark on news of further draw in U.S. exchange-certified stocks but the rally quickly ran out of steam.
Options traders said buying a January $1,350 put financed by a sell on March $1,450 call was a good strategy for bears. It would provide downside protection for a net cost of $10-15.
The market was also tuned to New York options expiry with some delta hedging expected in December $1.20 calls if the market rallies.
In London, March calls saw light trading on $1,400 and $1,450 with steady volatilities of 24-25 percent.
Cocoa volatilities tumbled to historic lows with spot December options, still with more than two weeks to run, commanding an implied 11 percent from a peak of 31 percent.
"It seems worth buying purely on the basis that the market will give you ample opportunity to trade against it," said trade house Sucden in a daily cocoa options commentary.
Selling interest was intact on March 950 puts despite its poor premium.

A strategy for players who think the market may have bottomed out was buying the March calls of 1,050-1,100 stg and selling 950 puts, which overlaps with the contract low of 951 stg scored on Wednesday, according to traders.
This view was fortified by the market's surprise bounce after an initial pounding on Wednesday on news of a quarter-point rise in UK interest rates.
Few March spreads were traded at 1,000-1,025 calls with volatilities trading down to 16 pct from 19 last week.
Interest in the white sugar options market remained muted with just 100 lots of second-month March traded in equal amounts of $300 puts and $320 calls.
The bearish sentiment seen for nearby futures values had prompted players to look at taking downside cover at higher strike puts, traders said.
"There's a bit of interest in the March puts at $310 and $320 -- if people buy those they can get downside cover and there are a few bears in the camp," said one options trader.
December white sugar options are scheduled to expire on Friday.
-- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8072
